subject: revealToAll + partial:true lets a client harvest the full answer key, then score 100%
description:
PRE-EXISTING, NOT caused by #295. gradeQuiz reveals results[i].correctAnswer + explanation on a partial call whenever the key doc has revealToAll:true (functions/index.js:1801,1806). InstantQuizGrader.gradeOne documents this dependency in its own comment (_app/components/InstantQuizGrader.js:105-129). A scripted client can therefore call gradeQuiz with {partial:true} once per index, collect every correct answer, then submit a full attempt with all of them and score 100% with zero knowledge. 122 of 621 quiz_keys entries carry revealToAll:true. Surfaced by Nancy during the #295 design review 2026-08-07; she framed it as an escalation caused by pool-draw, but it is not -- a non-pooled revealToAll quiz is already a guaranteed 100%, so pooling does not make it worse. Logged separately so #295 is not blocked by it. FIX DIRECTION (needs operator): partial reveal is the whole point of instant-feedback pedagogy, so the remedy is probably rate/sequence enforcement (server records which questions were served and refuses to reveal an index the student has not been shown this attempt) rather than removing the reveal. That needs the same server-side attempt record as a true server-side draw, so it likely shares a solution with the pool-draw identity problem.
[2026-08-08 04:07] REPRODUCED 2026-08-08 in functions/tests/reveal-harvest-exploit.test.js (no creds, no network, runs in CI): harvested 12/12 answers in 12 partial calls, then scored 100% with zero knowledge; blind guessing on the same quiz scores 25%. Partial calls leak the explanation too, not just the index. Confirms Nancy's own caveat that this is NOT a pool-draw escalation. NO FIX BUILT -- it changes the security model of a Cloud Function grading 122 quizzes, so per CLAUDE.md rule 7 it needs a green light. Design in _docs/operations/297-reveal-harvest-design.md: FIRST ANSWER WINS -- record the answer submitted at reveal time in users/{uid}/quiz_progress/{quizId}, and on the full submission score the recorded answer instead of the resubmitted one. Verified behaviour-neutral for honest students by reading all 4 quizzes that make partial calls: the question locks after feedback (re-enabled only on grading failure), there is no back navigation (currentQ++ only, no prevBtn), and gradeAll(picks) sends exactly what gradeOne already graded. Cost: 1 read + 1 write per partial call, which contradicts the existing index.js decision that partial calls should not write -- flagged in the doc rather than overturned quietly. OPEN QUESTION worth deciding together with this: the same document could carry a served:[] field and give #295's pool-draw its authoritative draw, unblocking poolSize.
